- Outcomes, above the wire: the evaluation harness (`pnpm eval`) runs eight scripted scenarios (simple edit, interrupted task, stale observation, two actors, unavailable control, lost response, navigation, human handoff) against the reference app in four variants (generic markup, accessible names, basic tools, AXE), scores success against the app's own state and history, and re-runs after a controlled UI change. Copy its shape for your own tasks as a regression layer. Its results are scripted agents doing the best an interface allows, not model performance; the model-driven runner exists and refuses to start without explicit configuration.
- DOM mirror: for every observed row, `document.querySelector(surfaceSelector(row.id))` finds exactly one element, its `aria-label` equals the row's `name`, and an unavailable action carries `aria-disabled` with `data-surface-reason` ([S-DOM-1], [S-DOM-3]).
- Honesty: run `lintAgentText` over your names and reasons in a unit test, so a persuasive or agent-directed string fails in CI rather than being dropped by the bridge at runtime; run `lintAction` (or `axe validate`) so an unsupported schema construct is an error before a payload meets it.
- Drift and vocabulary, in this repository: `cd packages/testing && pnpm exec vitest run test/drift.test.ts`. Every inline code span in `spec/`, `docs/`, and the README that looks like a wire name must be in `spec/VOCABULARY.md`, and every vocabulary name must be mentioned in the docs and used in source. In another repository, `checkVocabularyDrift({ root, docPaths, allowlistPath, maxAllowlist })` from `@summationai/axe-testing` does the same.
- [packages/surface/test/auto.test.ts](https://github.com/summationai/agent-experience/blob/main/packages/surface/test/auto.test.ts): derivation, keys, acting, revision and staleness (the live table, `data-surface-ignore`, the relay indicator), the approval gate and the approver, configuration, coverage; [packages/surface/test/auto-react.test.ts](https://github.com/summationai/agent-experience/blob/main/packages/surface/test/auto-react.test.ts) and [packages/surface/test/auto-axe.test.ts](https://github.com/summationai/agent-experience/blob/main/packages/surface/test/auto-axe.test.ts): the provider and the generic tools.
- [packages/relay/test/relay.test.ts](https://github.com/summationai/agent-experience/blob/main/packages/relay/test/relay.test.ts): tabs, tokens, origins, tenants, approvals, Stop, `rekey`, revisions across reloads, sensitive fields kept out of frames, and the indicator marked `data-surface-ignore`.
- [packages/surface/test/surface.test.ts](https://github.com/summationai/agent-experience/blob/main/packages/surface/test/surface.test.ts): the two-participant, target-validation, freeze, and ledger tests, one per rule id.
- [packages/surface/test/preconditions.test.ts](https://github.com/summationai/agent-experience/blob/main/packages/surface/test/preconditions.test.ts): act ordering, the handler's own precondition, stale reports, and two concurrent requests through AXE.
- [packages/surface/test/auth.test.ts](https://github.com/summationai/agent-experience/blob/main/packages/surface/test/auth.test.ts): every protected path over HTTP, scoped surfaces, sensitive fields, the ledger text policy.
- [packages/surface/test/react-mounted.test.ts](https://github.com/summationai/agent-experience/blob/main/packages/surface/test/react-mounted.test.ts): the hooks mounted under jsdom.
- [packages/surface/test/granularity.test.ts](https://github.com/summationai/agent-experience/blob/main/packages/surface/test/granularity.test.ts): both granularities on one script, paging and cursors.
- [packages/surface/test/axe.test.ts](https://github.com/summationai/agent-experience/blob/main/packages/surface/test/axe.test.ts): the bridge tests, ending with a surface served through AXE passing the conformance suite including the live checks.
- [packages/surface/test/dom.test.ts](https://github.com/summationai/agent-experience/blob/main/packages/surface/test/dom.test.ts): `surfaceAttributes`, `surfaceSelector`, `describeEntry`.
- [packages/core/test/approvals.test.ts](https://github.com/summationai/agent-experience/blob/main/packages/core/test/approvals.test.ts): the approval lifecycle, one test per rule.
- [packages/core/test/operations.test.ts](https://github.com/summationai/agent-experience/blob/main/packages/core/test/operations.test.ts): concurrent calls and tokens with barriers, lost responses, leases, crash recovery by `operationId`.
- [examples/plan-review/test/server.test.ts](https://github.com/summationai/agent-experience/blob/main/examples/plan-review/test/server.test.ts): login, tenants, two people, a person's change between observe and act, a lost response, reconnection, approvals, takeover.
- [docs/evaluation.md](docs/evaluation.html): the harness, what it measures and does not, how to run it, the recorded run.
- [docs/examples/testing/classes.test-example.ts](https://github.com/summationai/agent-experience/blob/main/docs/examples/testing/classes.test-example.ts): an action under test with `createTestClient`, `invokeAction`, and `samplePayload`.
- [docs/examples/testing/drift.ts](https://github.com/summationai/agent-experience/blob/main/docs/examples/testing/drift.ts): the drift check as a script for another repository.
- [packages/testing/test/drift.test.ts](https://github.com/summationai/agent-experience/blob/main/packages/testing/test/drift.test.ts): the drift test itself.

## What is and is not claimed

Each kind of evidence, kept apart. None is evidence of production readiness, agent adoption, or commercial value.

- Protocol conformance: `axe conformance` checks the wire behavior it can exercise against a URL. A skipped check was not verified, and conformance is not a security review.
- Tested security properties: token binding, atomic operations, client credential and destination rules, poll and Surface authorization, CSRF, site principals, write preconditions, MCP identity, and limits are pinned by named tests listed per property in review items 01 to 12 ([docs/review/2026-09-24/README.md](docs/review/2026-09-24/README.html)). They cover this code, not your deployment or your handlers.
- Measured task effectiveness: [docs/evaluation.md](docs/evaluation.html) measures scripted outcomes on the reference app, written by the SDK's authors, as a regression signal. It is not model performance; no model-driven run, second application, or pilot has been run.
- Easy mode: the derivation, the config, coverage, the provider, and the relay are pinned by unit tests under jsdom, a headless browser check (`pnpm --filter @summationai/axe-surface test:browser`), and the relay's integration tests, and were tried end to end on the Plan Board demo and the reference application. Names and risks are heuristics over English words and page structure; a derived surface is as good as the page's accessibility semantics plus its reviewed config.
- Heuristic checks: the honesty lints are regular expressions over known phrasings and the parity check is a sample. An audit score is a lint with a live smoke test: not a security review, and not evidence of task success, adoption, or value.
- Payment and identity kinds are payload shapes. A valid `payment.card` payload is well-formed, not an accepted payment; charging and verification stay with the site, and no agent wallet is known to produce these kinds.
- [README.md](docs/repo/README.html): "What is and is not claimed".
- [docs/testing-and-conformance.md](docs/testing-and-conformance.html#what-conformance-does-not-show): the evidence table and what conformance does not show.
- [docs/audit.md](docs/audit.html#what-a-score-does-not-mean): how skips are scored and what a score does not mean.

## Reading order

Repository paths below map to the published site as `docs/<name>.md` to `site/dist/docs/<name>.html`, `spec/<NAME>.md` to `site/dist/docs/spec/<NAME>.html`, and root Markdown files to `site/dist/docs/repo/<NAME>.html`.

- [docs/getting-started.md](docs/getting-started.html): start here: add Surface with `axe surface init`, register the application with the provider, then "Serve actions over AXE".
- [docs/auto-surface.md](docs/auto-surface.html): easy mode: the three tiers, what is derived, safety defaults, `SurfaceConfig`, coverage, the generic tools.
- [docs/relay.md](docs/relay.html): an agent outside the browser in a person's live tab: local development, approvals and Stop, tenant switches, production with OAuth, the security model.
- [docs/surface.md](docs/surface.html): the model under both tiers, and the declared tier: registration, observe and act, preconditions, granularity, authorization, the DOM mirror, React, where a surface runs.
- [spec/SURFACE.md](docs/spec/SURFACE.html): the contract you are implementing against; read sections 2, 5, 9.1, and 10 before configuring easy mode, and 6 (with 6.1) and 9 before writing an adapter.
- [docs/reference-app.md](docs/reference-app.html): a runnable application with both execution modes, approvals, and browser tests.
- [docs/live-state.md](docs/live-state.html): the protocol side of revisions and availability.
- [docs/concepts.md](docs/concepts.html): manifest, action, display, the result envelope, the escalation ladder, idempotency, auth, risk.
- [docs/designing-actions.md](docs/designing-actions.html): decomposing a human flow into actions, writing descriptions for a model, choosing risk, anti-patterns.
- [docs/human-oversight.md](docs/human-oversight.html): approvals bound to the call, the principal, the tenant, and the state.
- [docs/schemas.md](docs/schemas.html): the supported JSON Schema subset, how unsupported constructs fail, refinements, input as sent.
- [docs/generating.md](docs/generating.html): when the application already has an OpenAPI document, typed functions, or a tRPC router.
- [docs/integrations/express.md](docs/integrations/express.html): mounting with `axeExpress`, passing the session in, body parsers, proxies.
- [docs/integrations/next.md](docs/integrations/next.html): `axeNext` for the App Router, `axeNextPages` for the Pages API.
- [docs/integrations/fetch.md](docs/integrations/fetch.html): `axeFetch` for Hono, Remix, Workers, Bun, Deno, SvelteKit.
- [docs/auth.md](docs/auth.html): `none`, `site`, and `user` modes; passing a session in; cookie sessions and the request policy.
- [docs/mcp.md](docs/mcp.html): the derived MCP server over stdio and HTTP, authentication, freshness, retries, elicitation, the Apps view.
- [docs/webmcp.md](docs/webmcp.html): a surface offered to the browser's own agent, and the fallback.
- [docs/testing-and-conformance.md](docs/testing-and-conformance.html): unit tests, conformance locally and in CI, every check, what conformance does not show.
- [docs/evaluation.md](docs/evaluation.html): the outcome harness and its recorded run.
- [docs/deploying.md](docs/deploying.html): production configuration, stores, limits, and rollout.
- [docs/security.md](docs/security.html): what the SDK mitigates and what the site must do.
- [spec/AXE-PROTOCOL.md](docs/spec/AXE-PROTOCOL.html): the normative protocol; sections 5.4 (schemas), 6.4 and 6.5 (browser requests, limits), 9.3 (approvals), 12.2 (operations), 17.1 (agent destinations), 21 (live state), and 22 (MCP).
- [spec/KINDS.md](docs/spec/KINDS.html): the well-known kinds an unavailable control can `requires`.
- [spec/EVENTS.md](docs/spec/EVENTS.html): analytics events and action events, including `surface.act` and the approval events.
- [spec/VOCABULARY.md](docs/spec/VOCABULARY.html): every wire name, CLI command, and API identifier; the drift test enforces it.
- [docs/for-agent-builders.md](docs/for-agent-builders.html): the agent side, if you also write the consumer: freshness, where credentials go, timeouts and budgets.
- [docs/api/README.md](docs/api/README.html): the generated API reference, per package.
- [DECISIONS.md](docs/repo/DECISIONS.html): why each non-obvious choice was made; the Relay, Easy mode, Integration (the four-step path), The ledger as the one history, Surface, Live state, Generate, Client trust, MCP over HTTP, Limits and schema boundaries, Existing agent interfaces, and Human oversight and execution modes sections are the ones an integrator needs.
- [CHANGELOG.md](docs/repo/CHANGELOG.html): what shipped, by area and by review item, with migrations.
- [ROADMAP.md](docs/repo/ROADMAP.html): six ordered priorities, each labeled open SDK primitive or commercial hypothesis, and what v0 deliberately leaves out.

## API at a glance

Exact exported names, checked against `packages/*/src`. Wire names are spelled as in [spec/VOCABULARY.md](docs/spec/VOCABULARY.html).

- `@summationai/axe-core`: `createAXE`, `action`, `ok`, `needsInput`, `handoff`, `pending`, `fail`, `unavailable`, `requestApproval`, `APPROVAL_REQUIRED`, `APPROVAL_TTL_SECONDS`, `kinds`, `accept`, `customKind`, `withMimeTypes`, `lintAgentText`, `lintAction`, `lintManifest`, `resolveDisplay`, `consoleSink`, `otelSink`, `combineSinks`, `MemoryTokenStore`, `MemoryIdempotencyStore`, `validateJsonSchema`, `toJsonSchema`, `isZodSchema`, `evaluateRequestPolicy`, `isAcceptedOrigin`, `isJsonContentType`, `WIRE`, `z`; from `@summationai/axe-core/node`: `jsonlFileSink`, `SqliteIdempotencyStore` (`prune`); from `@summationai/axe-core/json-schema`: `schemaProblems`, `isBacktrackingPattern`, `SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_KEYWORDS`. On the `AXE` instance: `register`, `addProvider` (an `ActionProvider` may declare `onResult(ctx: ProviderResultContext, result)`, called with the results of its own actions), `onActionsChanged`, `describe`, `describeLive`, `fetchHandler`, `handle`, `completeHandoff`, `getHandoff`, `approveHandoff`, `cancelHandoff`, `maxBodyBytes`. `createAXE` options that matter here: `revision`, `secret`, `tokenStore`, `idempotencyStore` (`get`, `claim`, `complete`, `release`), `idempotencyTtlSeconds`, `operationLeaseSeconds`, `maxBodyBytes`, `requireIdempotencyKey`, `requestPolicy` (`requireJsonContentType`, `trustedOrigins`, `originCheck`), `cors`, `tenant`, `manifestCacheSeconds`, `onRequest`, `onResult`, `onError`, `onEvent`, `onActionEvent`; `auth: { modes, userLoginUrl, authenticate, verifySiteKey }`, optional, default `{ modes: ["none"] }`. `action()` takes `availability` and `approvalState` beside `input`, `output`, `handler`, `onContinue`, `onResume`, `onPoll`; handler contexts carry `operationId`, `expectedRev`, and `siteKey`, and `onResume` receives `approval`. Memory stores take `now`, `maxEntries`, `sweepIntervalMs` and have `sweep()` and `close()`. Types include `IdempotencyStore`, `TokenStore`, `SiteKeyContext`, `HandoffView`, `HandoffDecision`, `ApprovalGrant`, `RequestPolicyConfig`.
- `@summationai/axe-surface`: `createSurface({ app, now, ledger: { max, text, redact }, revision, toJsonSchema })`; on a surface: `configure`, `register`, `unregister`, `reconcile`, `freeze`, `seedRev`, `setRev`, `currentRev`, `bump`, `onChange`, `setObjects`, `observe`, `act`, `ledger`, `record`, `expose`, `subscribe`, `get`, `entries`, `registryVersion`, `availability`, `revisionMode`, `attributesFor`, `reset`; the module-level `surface` with the first sixteen of those bound; `SurfaceConflict`, `surfaceAttributes`, `surfaceSelector`, `describeEntry`, `SURFACE_ATTRIBUTES`. Types: `Entry`, `ActionEntry`, `FieldEntry` (with `sensitive`), `CollectionEntry`, `Effect`, `Availability`, `HandoffSpec`, `Observation`, `ObservedEntry`, `ActRequest`, `ActResult`, `ActOutput`, `ActContext`, `HandlerReport` (`changed`, `rev`, `conflict`), `RevisionMode`, `SchemaLike`, `SchemaConverter`, `SurfaceAttributeUpdate`, `LedgerEntry` (with `textHash`, `ignoredRev`, `source`, `expectedRev`), `LedgerSource`, `EntryTier` (an entry's and observe row's `tier`), `RecordRequest`, `LedgerQuery`, `LedgerOptions`, `LedgerTextPolicy`, `Op`, `EntryKind`, `Thaw`.
- `@summationai/axe-surface/react`: `SurfaceProvider` (props `config`, `flag`, `enabled`, `expose`, `webMcp`, `root`, `surface`, `location`, `onReady(handle)` returning an optional cleanup, and the `autoSurface` options `observe`, `route`, `hidden`, `revision`, `layout`, `now`), `useAutoSurface(options)` (returns the handle or null), `useAutoSurfaceHandle()` (the nearest provider's handle, null before start and on the server), `useSurface(entry, deps, target?)`, `useSurfaceProps(entry, deps, target?)`, `toSurfaceProps`; types `SurfaceProviderProps`, `UseAutoSurfaceOptions`, `SurfaceProps`.
- `@summationai/axe-surface/auto`: `autoSurface({ root, surface, config, observe: { debounceMs, settle: { quietMs, timeoutMs } }, expose, route, hidden, revision, layout, now })` returning an `AutoSurfaceHandle` (`surface`, `refresh`, `coverage`, `configure`, `config`, `approve(id, { uses, ttlMs })`, `elementFor`, `metaFor`, `route`, `expose`, `stop`); `formatCoverage`, `checkConfig`, `autoDomains`, `autoMarkOf`, `globMatch`, `accessibleName`, `roleOf`, `defaultRoute`, `DEFAULT_LEXICON`, `NAVIGATE_ENTRY_ID`, `IGNORE_ATTRIBUTE` (`data-surface-ignore`), `AUTO_META`. `APPROVER` is exported but not for applications: it is the shared symbol (`Symbol.for("axe.surface.approver")`) through which a trusted in-page channel, the relay's panel, grants a derived approval gate; it is not in the vocabulary, and wiring it to anything an agent can reach defeats the gate. Types `SurfaceConfig`, `SurfaceRule`, `SurfaceMatch`, `SurfaceGroup`, `SurfacePolicy`, `PolicyDecision`, `AutoHandler`, `AutoHandlerContext`, `AutoSurfaceOptions`, `AutoEntryMeta`, `Coverage`, `CoverageEntry`, `CoverageGap`, `GapKind`, `StaleRule`, `RiskLexicon`, `Confidence`, `NameFrom`.
- `@summationai/axe-surface/axe`: `surfaceActions(source, { namespace, auth, read, authFor, template, actor, run, fields, onError, redactEvent, observe })` returning a `SurfaceBridge` (`actions`, `get`, `onChange`, `onResult`, `actionNameFor`, `entryIdFor`); `domainActions(source, { namespace, domains, auth, read, template, observe, ... })` returning a `DomainBridge` (`actions`, `get`, `onChange`, `onResult`, `actionFor`, `covered`), with `DomainActionSpec`; `scopedSurfaces({ create, key, max, idleMs, now, onEvict })` returning `{ resolve, keyFor, get, delete, size }`; `entrySlug`; `SURFACE_ACT_EVENT` (the string `surface.act`); `autoActions(handleOrSurface, options)`, `domainActions` over `autoDomains()` with the handle's config groups. `source` is a surface or a resolver `(context: SurfaceContext) => Surface | null`.
- `@summationai/axe-surface/webmcp`: `exposeWebMcp(surface, { modelContext, prefix, actor, unavailable, observe, run, requestApproval, onError })` returning a `WebMcpHandle` (`supported`, `reason`, `ready`); `webMcpToolNames`; types `WebMcpApprovalRequest`, `WebMcpApprovalDecision`.
- `@summationai/axe-relay/client`: `connectRelay(surface, { url, token, getToken, onStatus, indicator, requireApproval, approvalTtlMs, backoff, WebSocket, storage, describe })` returning a `RelayConnection` (`tabId`, `status()`, `stop()`, `approve(id)`, `deny(id)`, `rekey(token?)`); `localMcpService(serviceUrl?)`, `LOCAL_MCP_SERVICE_URL`, `devToken(relayUrl)`, `tabEndpoint`; types `RelayStatus` (`state`, `tabId`, `principal`, `pairingCode`, `approvals`, `reason`), `RelayState`, `RelayApproval`, `ConnectRelayOptions`.
- `@summationai/axe-relay/token`: `mintRelayToken({ principal, tenant, ttl, audience, claims }, secret)`, `verifyRelayToken(token, secret, { audience })` (claims or null), `MAX_RELAY_TOKEN_TTL`, `RELAY_AUDIENCE` (`axe-relay`).
- `@summationai/axe-relay/server`: `createRelay({ secret, authenticateTab, origins, audience, tenants, agentAuth: { verifier, identify, requiredScopes, resource, resourceMetadataUrl }, devPairing, devPrincipal, devAgentKey, namespace, domains, baseUrl, name, description, actTimeoutMs, syncTimeoutMs, reconnectGraceMs, tabRetentionMs, onFrame, onEvent })` returning a `Relay` (`axe`, `devAgentKey`, `listen({ host, port })`, `attach(server)`, `handle(request)`, `serveStdio({ as })`, `tabs(who)`, `refresh(who, tabId)`, `close()`); also `relayActor`, `originMatcher`, `isLoopbackAddress`, and the token functions. MCP tools `relay_tabs`, `relay_select-tab`, `relay_pair` (development), then `<namespace>_observe`, `_set-field`, `_run-control`, `_load-more`, `_ledger` (namespace `surface` by default). `@summationai/axe-relay/cli`: `runRelayCli`.
- `@summationai/axe-generate`: `fromOpenAPI`, `fromFunctions`, `fromTRPCRouter`, `generate`, `registerGenerated`, `formatWarnings`, `jsonSchemaToZod`.
- Adapters: `axeExpress`, `toWebRequest`, `sendWebResponse` (`@summationai/axe-express`); `axeNext`, `axeNextPages` (`@summationai/axe-next`); `axeFetch`, `isAxePath` (`@summationai/axe-fetch`).
- `@summationai/axe-client`: `discover`, `AXEClient` (`discover`, `invoke`, `continue`, `resume`, `poll`, `run`, `state`, `live`, `allowed`, `manifest`, `action`, `checkDestination`, `refresh`, `ensureFresh`, `isManifestStale`, `onManifestChange`), `isOk`, `isNeedsInput`, `isNeedsHuman`, `isPending`, `isError`, `AXEClientError`, `AXETrustError`; options `auth`, `headers`, `trust` (`origins`, `allowCrossOrigin`, `allowHttp`, `destinationPolicy`), `manifestMaxAgeMs`, `timeoutMs`, `maxResponseBytes`, `retries`, `maxRetryAfterMs`, and per poll `maxWaitMs`, `maxPollAttempts`; `@summationai/axe-client/present`: `present`, `toMarkdown`, `toHTML`, `stateToMarkdown`.
- `@summationai/axe-mcp`: `createMcpServer(source, { client, pollBudgetMs, elicitation, apps })` (`refresh()` on the result), `serveStdio`, `serveHttp(derived, { sessions, auth, clientFor, allowedOrigins, allowSharedCredentials })` (`close()`, `sessionCount`), `protectedResourceMetadata`, `toolNameFor`, `formatResult`, `isSensitiveAccept`, `toFormSchema`.
- `@summationai/axe-testing`: `runConformance`, `formatConformanceTable`, `runAudit`, `formatAuditTable`, `formatAuditHtml`, `checkVocabularyDrift`, `formatDriftReport`, `createTestClient`, `invokeAction`, `samplePayload`, `REQUIREMENTS`, `WEIGHTS`.
- CLI `axe`: `axe surface init [--dir] [--framework] [--mount] [--app-id] [--app-name] [--flag] [--flag-hook --flag-import] [--browser-only] [--relay <url>|--relay-dev] [--dry-run] [--yes] [--install] [--vendor]`, `axe surface coverage <url> [--auth] [--routes] [--max-pages] [--wait] [--playwright-from] [--json] [--out]`, `axe surface prompt`, `axe relay --dev [--stdio] [--port] [--origin]` (or `--stdio --principal --tenant --origin` with `AXE_RELAY_SECRET`; `--host`, `--dev-key`), `axe init`, `axe validate`, `axe inspect`, `axe preview`, `axe conformance`, `axe audit`, `axe mcp`, `axe generate`.
- Wire: paths `/.well-known/axe.json`, `/axe/manifest`, `/axe/actions`, `/axe/continue`, `/axe/resume`, `/axe/poll`, `/axe/state`; headers `AXE-Protocol`, `Retry-After`; statuses `ok`, `needs_input`, `needs_human`, `pending`, `error`; error codes `invalid_input`, `unauthorized`, `forbidden`, `not_found`, `conflict`, `rate_limited`, `unavailable`, `internal`, `unsupported`; reasons include `approval_required`, `json_required`, `cross_origin_refused`, `payload_too_large`; `details` fields `operationStatus`, `handoffStatus`; MCP tools `axe_continue`, `axe_resume`, `axe_poll`, `axe_state`, `axe_manifest`; Surface ops `CLICK`, `TOGGLE`, `TYPE_TEXT`, `SCROLL_DOWN`; DOM attributes `data-surface-id`, `data-surface-kind`, `data-surface-object`, `data-surface-reason`, `data-surface-navigation`, `aria-label`, `aria-disabled`, `aria-readonly`.

## What does not exist yet

- No AXE server in any language but TypeScript. A Python, Go, or Ruby middleware cannot serve the manifest with a package from this repository today; the planning grid, a Python application, proves its surface with the in-process harness above and serves nothing over HTTP yet. The two ways to serve it are an AXE runtime embedded in the middleware (a port) or a Node process that owns the surface. The wire protocol is JSON over HTTPS with JSON Schemas for every document under `spec/schemas/`, so a port is glue (serve a manifest, validate input against the supported subset, sign HMAC-SHA256 tokens bound to tenant and principal, claim operations atomically, apply the request policy, return envelopes), and `axe conformance` verifies a port the same way it verifies the reference ([docs/faq.md](docs/faq.html), "Can I use it from Python or Go?"; [ROADMAP.md](docs/repo/ROADMAP.html), "Multi-language SDKs").
- No Surface outside JavaScript. `act` runs in-process handlers, so a surface for a page rendered by a Python or Java backend lives in the page's JavaScript (`expose(window)`, `exposeWebMcp`) or in a Node process that owns the handlers and serves it through AXE.
- Production authentication for unattended mode has two boundaries: the MCP service verifies the agent's OAuth identity, and the application authenticates the provider browser. A connector may supply a silent, short-lived application session through `sessionFor`; otherwise the generic host pauses on Surface's `signed-out` state and gives the person a session-bound semantic form derived from the same browser's standard visible sign-in controls. The latter preserves a browser-package-only customer installation and keeps credentials out of MCP. `local-unattended` serves the same flow on loopback. Federated identity-provider redirects, file pickers, passkeys, hardware keys, camera/microphone challenges, and CAPTCHAs need a provider OAuth connector, a brokered session, or another application-supported method.
- Everything in memory in one process: the host's sessions and Stop holds, and the relay's tab records, pairings, and revocations, reset on restart; a host runs one Chromium and one browser context per active person, so route each person to one host process.
- One relay process, in memory: tab records, pairings, and revocations live in one process and reset on restart. Run one relay per deployment, or route each person's tabs and agent to the same process; there is no shared relay state across instances ([docs/relay.md](docs/relay.html), "Limits").
- The relay's approval gate is in the page: a script already running in the page can press Approve, as it could click any control. Approval requests (and acts refused because the tab was stopped) are decided before the page's `surface.act`, so they are not in the page ledger; the act that runs after approval is, and the relay's `onEvent` stream records connections, refusals, Stop, and pairing.
- Easy mode's risk lexicon is English only (extend or replace it with `lexicon`); a page in another language gets view and commit words wrong and more controls fall to "not recognized", which is `high`. The name computation stops short of the full accessible-name algorithm for embedded controls in labels and for generated content, and the scan cannot see canvas drawing, charts without accessible data, cross-origin frames, unrendered rows of a virtualized list, closed shadow roots, or handlers on elements with no role (coverage reports each one it detects).
- Easy mode has been tried on the Plan Board demo and the reference application (the reference application also end to end through `axe host`, headless, with a scripted MCP client: [docs/review/2026-09-25/unattended-e2e.md](docs/review/2026-09-25/unattended-e2e.html)). The Summation integration has exposed a concrete root-mount requirement: if Surface mounts inside `AppShell`, both `/login/organizations` and `TenantSwitchModal` occur before it and a hidden host deadlocks waiting for a connection. The integration prompt now mounts one authenticated-or-injected provider at the root. A full model-driven Summation run through login, tenant choice, and report completion still must be exercised after that consuming-app upgrade.
- A collection without `more` has no action of its own; it stays a row of `<ns>.observe` ([S-AXE-6]).
- Nothing is published to npm; 0.1.0 is unreleased. See Packaging for tarballs.
- Surface bindings for React only. Easy mode's `autoSurface` is framework-free and reads any rendered DOM (Vue, Svelte, Angular, Web Components, plain HTML), and `axe surface init` has a plain-HTML setup; declared registration outside React uses the framework-free `register`, `unregister`, `reconcile`, `subscribe`, and `attributesFor` directly.
- Adapters for Express and Connect, Next.js, and Web-standard fetch handlers only. Fastify and Koa have no adapter of their own; `toWebRequest` and `sendWebResponse` from `@summationai/axe-express` are exported for writing one.
- One surface per page, or one per caller through a resolver (or one per tab through the relay), in one process's memory: the ledger is bounded and not persisted (the `surface.act` action events are the durable channel), and there is no shared registry across processes.
- One site-wide revision. A per-entry revision with a per-entry precondition is proposed in [DECISIONS.md](docs/repo/DECISIONS.html) ("The revision stays global; a per-entry precondition is a proposal, not code"), with measurements, and not implemented; the manifest has an `ETag`, but no action or resource has a revision of its own.
- Stores: `SqliteIdempotencyStore` is single-host; the Redis scripts are typechecked, not executed in CI, and can lose a claim on failover; a PostgreSQL port is described, not tested. `TokenStore` has no compare-and-set, so two simultaneous approval decisions or handoff completions can both succeed (last write wins).
- MCP HTTP sessions live in one process's memory, stateless clients get no `tools/list_changed` and no elicitation, and there is no background manifest refresh or `EventStore` replay.
- WebMCP and MCP Apps are untested in real hosts: the WebMCP adapter is tested against a fake that implements the draft's documented shape, not in a real browser, and the MCP Apps view under jsdom with a stand-in host, not in a shipping host.
- No pilot has run and no model-driven evaluation has run (of easy mode or of anything else); [docs/pilot-plan.md](docs/pilot-plan.html) is a plan and every commercial hypothesis in [ROADMAP.md](docs/repo/ROADMAP.html) is untested.
- No browser-driving agent ships here. `expose(window)` publishes the surface; the code that drives a page from `window.__surface` is the agent's.
- No OAuth 2.1 authorization server (`@summationai/axe-mcp` and the hosted service are resource servers that verify tokens yours issued), no manifest signing, no agent attestation, no webhooks or push, no streaming results, no server-side flow state machine, and no hosted app registry. The repository now includes a portable ChatGPT/Codex plugin package, but it is a source template until configured with a real deployed HTTPS endpoint and submitted through the platform review flow; each remaining gap has its reason and v0 substitute in [ROADMAP.md](docs/repo/ROADMAP.html).
- The honesty lints are regular expressions over known phrasings and the parity check is a spot-check ([docs/security.md](docs/security.html#known-gaps), "Known gaps").
- `axe generate` reads JSON only (no YAML), converts a deliberate subset of JSON Schema with a warning naming each dropped constraint, and skips cookie parameters and non-JSON request bodies with a warning.
